o: Only flush it, as flushing removes any contamination on its own
Return it to supply quickly so customers are not without water
Disinfect it, then flush it, before returning it to normal use
Record the work and move on without treating the pipe
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Disinfection is required after work that could have contaminated the system; the section is disinfected, then flushed, before being returned to normal supply.

n.1: Speed does not override the need to disinfect potentially contaminated pipework before use.
n.0: Flushing alone does not disinfect; it removes loose material but does not inactivate organisms.
n.3: Recording is necessary but does not make a potentially contaminated main safe to use.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: While inspecting a cold water storage tank you find it visibly dirty, with debris and biofilm. What does finding a tank in this condition require?
o: Leaving it until the next scheduled annual inspection
Adding a little more disinfectant to the incoming supply
Simply topping the tank up with fresh water
Cleaning and disinfection of the tank
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Finding a tank or system dirty is a trigger for cleaning and disinfection; the tank is cleaned out and disinfected rather than left in a fouled state.

n.2: Topping up does not remove the debris and biofilm already present.
n.0: A known dirty tank should not be left uncontrolled until a future date.
n.1: Dosing the supply does not clean an already-fouled tank; it must be cleaned and disinfected.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Following a suspected or confirmed outbreak associated with a water system, disinfection is:
o: Entirely optional, depending largely on just how many people were actually affected
Unnecessary, if the system is due to be replaced soon anyway
Only needed once the outbreak has completely passed on its own
One of the required responses, alongside investigating and correcting the cause
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: A suspected or confirmed outbreak, or a loss of control, is a trigger for disinfection; the system is disinfected and the cause investigated and corrected.

n.0: Disinfection is a required response to an outbreak, not an optional one scaled to numbers affected.
n.2: Action is taken to regain control, not deferred until after the outbreak resolves itself.
n.1: A pending replacement does not remove the immediate need to disinfect and control the risk.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: After a section of pipework has been disinfected by chlorination and the contact time is complete, what must be done before it goes back into normal use?
o: Nothing further is needed at all; the disinfectant can simply be left in the pipe
Raise the disinfectant dose again just to be completely certain that it worked
Cap the ends and leave the whole system pressurised with the chemical inside
Isolate and flush it so the disinfectant is cleared to normal supply quality
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Once the contact time is complete the system is flushed to remove the disinfectant and return the water to normal supply quality before it is used.

n.0: Leaving high-strength disinfectant in a system used for drinking or washing is unsafe.
n.1: Re-dosing does not clear the disinfectant; flushing to normal supply is required.
n.2: Trapping the chemical in the pipe does not return it to usable supply quality.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Before handling and dosing the disinfection chemicals for a chlorination job, what should govern how you protect yourself?
o: Whatever gloves happen to be in the van that day
A quick look at the container to see if it seems hazardous
The COSHH assessment and the required PPE for that chemical
Personal preference, since experienced operatives know the risks
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Disinfection chemicals must be handled safely under COSHH, using the assessment and the PPE it specifies, because concentrated disinfectants are hazardous to health.

n.1: A glance at the container is not a substitute for the COSHH assessment and specified controls.
n.0: PPE must match the chemical hazard, not simply be whatever is to hand.
n.3: Safe handling follows the COSHH controls, not individual preference or assumed familiarity.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: During a monitoring check you record a temperature reading that is outside the required range. What is the correct action?
o: Re-write the reading so that it falls neatly back within the range
Correct the reading only if somebody else happens to notice it later
Ignore it entirely, since a single reading is unlikely to matter
Record it, then escalate to the responsible person so the cause can be corrected
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: An out-of-range reading or fault must be recorded, escalated to the responsible person, and the underlying cause corrected; findings are never altered or ignored.

n.0: Altering a reading is falsification of a safety record and is never acceptable.
n.1: Correct handling does not depend on whether anyone notices; it must always be recorded.
n.2: An out-of-range reading is a sign of possible loss of control and must be acted on.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: How should microbiological sampling be regarded in relation to temperature control on a hot and cold water system?
o: As something that only matters after a system has failed
As a supplement that supports but does not replace it
As a full replacement, so temperatures need not be checked
As proof the system is safe for the whole year ahead
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Sampling supplements temperature control; it provides additional information but does not replace maintaining and monitoring the correct temperatures as the primary control.

n.0: Sampling has a supporting role in routine monitoring, not only after a failure.
n.2: Sampling gives a snapshot; it cannot replace ongoing temperature control.
n.3: A sample reflects conditions at one moment and does not guarantee safety for a whole year.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: When carrying out a disinfection, whose method should determine the doses, contact times and steps you follow?
o: The written scheme or method statement for the task
Your own judgement, adjusting the method as you see fit on site
The shortest process that still looks thorough
Whatever the previous operative did last time, from memory
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Disinfection must be carried out in line with the written scheme or method statement, which sets the doses, contact times and steps so the work is done consistently and safely.

n.1: Ad hoc changes on site can undermine the process; the written method must be followed.
n.3: Relying on memory of past jobs is not a controlled method; the written scheme governs the work.
n.2: Cutting the process short to save time can leave the system inadequately disinfected.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: You are asked on site to carry out part of a disinfection procedure that you have not been trained to do. What should you do?
o: Do not work beyond your competence; tell the responsible person
Watch a quick video on your own phone and then get on with it
Guess the doses from your experience of similar tasks
Attempt it anyway so that the job is not delayed
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: You must not work beyond your competence; unfamiliar or untrained tasks are referred to the responsible person so a competent person carries them out.

n.3: Carrying out safety-critical work you are not trained for risks getting it wrong and harming users.
n.1: An informal video is not adequate training for safety-critical disinfection work.
n.2: Guessing doses on a disinfection job can leave it ineffective or create a chemical hazard.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: A colleague suggests signing off a failed disinfection check as a pass to avoid the paperwork of a re-test. This is:
o: Acceptable, provided the failure was only a marginal one
Never acceptable, as it hides risk and falsifies records
Fine, as long as the responsible person is simply not told
A reasonable time-saving decision to make on a busy day
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: You must never ignore, hide or falsify a failed check. A failure must be recorded honestly and escalated so the cause is corrected, protecting people who use the water.

n.0: A marginal failure is still a failure and must be acted on.
n.2: Concealing a failure from the responsible person must not happen.
n.3: Falsifying a safety record is never justified by time pressure.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: In a chlorination disinfection, which combination best describes the method?
o: Add just about any amount of chlorine and then use the system straight away
A measured dose held for a set contact time, then flushed out
A single very high dose of chlorine left permanently sitting in the system
Heat every outlet in the whole building to a set temperature for a set time
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Chlorination uses a measured disinfectant dose maintained for a defined contact time, after which the system is flushed to return it to normal supply quality.

n.0: The dose must be measured and held for a contact time, not arbitrary.
n.2: The disinfectant is flushed out after the contact time, not left in.
n.3: Heating outlets describes thermal disinfection, not chlorination.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: After a disinfection is complete and the system has been flushed, before drinking or washing water is used from it, the water should be:
o: Used straight away, even if the disinfectant residual is still high
Kept isolated permanently as an ongoing safety precaution
Returned to normal supply quality, with the disinfectant cleared
Left standing for a full week regardless of its actual quality
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: The system is flushed until the water is returned to normal supply quality and the elevated disinfectant is cleared, so it is safe to use again.

n.0: Using water with a high disinfectant residual is unsafe; it must be flushed to normal supply first.
n.1: The point of the process is to return the system to use, not isolate it forever.
n.3: Leaving it standing does not clear the disinfectant; flushing to normal quality is required.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: A stored water system has been altered by adding new pipework and fittings. Before the altered system is used, it should be:
o: Left for the water company to decide whether to treat it
Checked only for leaks, with no disinfection
Disinfected, then flushed, before being returned to use
Used immediately as only part of it is new
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Altered systems are treated like new work: they are disinfected before use, then flushed and returned to normal supply, because alterations can introduce contamination.

n.3: Adding new pipework introduces potential contamination that must be dealt with before use.
n.0: Responsibility for treating the altered system lies with the duty holder, not deferred to others.
n.1: A leak check does not address microbiological contamination from the alteration work.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Monitoring shows that control measures have not been maintained and the system has experienced a loss of control. This situation is:
o: Only a concern if a positive water sample is later found somewhere on site
Not relevant to disinfection of the system in any way at all
A recognised trigger for disinfection and correction of the underlying cause
Best left alone until the next scheduled annual system review
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: A loss of control is one of the recognised triggers for disinfection; the system is disinfected and the reason control was lost is investigated and corrected.

n.0: Loss of control is itself a trigger; you do not wait for a positive sample.
n.1: Loss of control is directly relevant, as it is a defined trigger for disinfection.
n.3: A loss of control needs prompt action, not deferral to a future review.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Why is physically cleaning surfaces before disinfection so important where biofilm is present?
o: Because cleaning the system does away with the need to disinfect it at all
Because clean surfaces simply look a great deal more professional to the client
Because doing so makes the disinfectant last a lot longer in storage afterwards
Because biofilm and deposits can shield the organisms from the disinfectant
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Biofilm and deposits protect organisms from disinfectant; removing them first lets the disinfectant reach and inactivate the organisms, which is why you clean before you disinfect.

n.0: Cleaning does not replace disinfection; both steps are needed.
n.1: Appearance is not the reason; soiling shields organisms.
n.2: Cleaning has nothing to do with the disinfectant's shelf life.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: An operative opens a rarely used storage tank and finds slime coating the walls and a build-up of sludge. Beyond cleaning and disinfecting, what should also happen?
o: The slime is left in place because it protects the surface
Nothing further is needed, provided the operative tops up the chemical dose
The tank is closed up again quickly to avoid disturbing it
Record the finding and inform the responsible person so the cause is addressed
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: As well as cleaning and disinfecting, the finding is recorded and escalated to the responsible person so the underlying cause, such as stagnation, can be investigated and corrected.

n.0: Slime and sludge are contamination to be removed, not a protective layer.
n.1: Dosing does not clean the fouling or address why the tank became contaminated.
n.2: Closing the tank up hides a known problem instead of correcting it.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Part-way through a chlorination the measured disinfectant residual is well below the level required for the method. What should the operative do?
o: Assume it is close enough and move straight on to flushing
Complete the job anyway and record it as a normal and successful disinfection
Reduce the contact time to match the lower measured residual
Re-establish the required residual and hold it for the full contact time
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: The method depends on maintaining the required concentration for the contact time; if the residual drops, it must be brought back up and held for the full time before flushing.

n.0: Flushing before the residual is held leaves it inadequately disinfected.
n.1: Recording an under-dosed run as successful is inaccurate and unsafe.
n.2: Shortening the contact time undermines the disinfection, not fixes it.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: During a thermal disinfection, one outlet will not reach the required temperature even after running for a long time. The correct response is to:
o: Sign off the whole disinfection as fully complete anyway
Assume the outlet is fine, since the others reached temperature
Skip that one outlet and never mention it in the records
Record the fault and escalate it so the cause is investigated and properly corrected
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: An outlet that cannot reach temperature is a fault; it is recorded, escalated to the responsible person and the cause corrected, because that part of the system has not been disinfected.

n.0: The disinfection is not complete if an outlet never reached the required temperature.
n.2: Omitting the fault from records hides a real problem and is a form of falsification.
n.1: Each outlet must reach temperature in its own right; other outlets do not prove this one is safe.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: When a fault or out-of-range result is escalated to the responsible person, what is the ultimate aim of doing so?
o: To simply pass the paperwork on to someone more senior and then finish
To create a record that mainly protects the operative from any blame
To have the underlying cause corrected so that control is regained
To delay taking any real action until the next scheduled inspection is due
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Escalation exists so the responsible person can ensure the underlying cause is corrected and control regained, not merely to log a problem.

n.0: Escalation is about getting the cause fixed, not just handing off paperwork.
n.1: Protecting an individual is not the purpose; protecting water users is.
n.3: The aim is prompt correction of the cause, not delay until a later date.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Chlorinated water used in a disinfection must not simply be discharged in an uncontrolled way. Before disposal it should be:
o: Left sitting in the system entirely, so that it never needs disposing of at all
Tipped straight down the nearest drain regardless of its concentration
Handled and disposed of safely, following the method statement and any consents
Poured directly into the nearest watercourse simply to save a little bit of time
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: High-strength chlorinated water is hazardous; it is handled and disposed of safely in line with the method statement and any environmental requirements, not discharged uncontrolled.

n.0: Leaving the disinfectant in the system prevents the return to normal supply and is unsafe.
n.1: Tipping high-strength disinfectant to drain without regard to concentration can be harmful.
n.3: Discharging chlorinated water straight to a watercourse can harm the environment and breach consents.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Which of the following is NOT, on its own, a recognised trigger for disinfecting a water system?
o: A positive legionella result from a water sample
A slight change in the colour of the tank lid
Bringing a new or refurbished system into use
Finding a tank or the system dirty on inspection
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Recognised triggers include new or refurbished systems, contaminating work, a dirty tank, a positive result, and suspected or confirmed outbreaks. The colour of a tank lid is not a trigger.

n.0: A positive legionella result is a recognised trigger for disinfection.
n.2: Bringing a new or refurbished system into use is a recognised trigger for disinfection.
n.3: Finding a tank or system dirty is a recognised trigger for cleaning and disinfection.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Two operatives disagree on how long to hold the disinfectant during a chlorination. One says 'until it looks done', the other wants to follow the stated contact time. Who is right and why?
o: The first, because visual judgement of the water is quicker
Whoever is more senior, regardless of the written method
Neither, since the contact time does not affect the disinfection result at all
The second, because the stated contact time makes the process effective
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: The disinfectant must be held for the stated contact time; effectiveness depends on concentration maintained over that defined time, not on how the water looks.

n.0: Water does not visibly show when disinfection is complete; the stated contact time governs it.
n.2: Contact time is central to disinfection; without it the process is unreliable.
n.1: Seniority does not override the written method's stated contact time.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: Before returning a disinfected tank to normal use, which steps are carried out in the correct order?
o: Return to use first, then clean and disinfect if problems appear
Disinfect, return to use at once, then flush at a later date
Flush to normal supply quality first, then apply the dose
Clean, disinfect for the contact time, then flush before use
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: The correct order is to clean, then disinfect for the contact time, then isolate and flush the disinfectant out to normal supply quality before the tank is returned to use.

n.0: The system is made safe before use, not treated only if problems show.
n.1: The disinfectant must be flushed out before use, not later.
n.2: Flushing before dosing reverses the process.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: After a disinfection has been completed and flushed, confirmatory sampling is sometimes taken. What is the purpose of this sampling?
o: To prove that the operative carried out the whole job impressively quickly
To decide the final price of the entire job for the paying client
To remove the need to have controlled the disinfection itself properly
To check the disinfection worked and support returning to use
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Confirmatory sampling supplements the process by checking the disinfection achieved its aim and supporting the decision to return the system to use; it does not replace doing the disinfection correctly.

n.0: Sampling checks water quality, not the speed of the work.
n.1: Sampling is a technical check, not a commercial pricing exercise.
n.2: Sampling supports but does not replace controlled disinfection.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: A site manager pressures a subcontractor to sign the disinfection certificate for a task the subcontractor did not carry out and is not competent in. The subcontractor should:
o: Sign it anyway, because the site manager is clearly more senior than them
Decline to sign, as they must not certify work beyond their competence
Sign it, to keep up a good working relationship with the site manager
Sign it, but add a short note saying that they were unsure of it
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: You must not work or certify beyond your competence, and records must be honest. The subcontractor declines to sign and raises it with the responsible person.

n.0: Seniority does not make it acceptable to certify work beyond your competence.
n.2: Certifying work you did not do or are not competent in is dishonest and unsafe.
n.3: A note of uncertainty does not make an inappropriate signature acceptable.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: When decanting a concentrated disinfectant into a dosing container, what is the key safe practice under COSHH?
o: Wear the specified PPE and follow the safe handling controls
Smell the chemical first to confirm that it is the right one
Mix it with other cleaning chemicals to help make it go further
Work quickly with your bare hands so you keep a good grip
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Concentrated disinfectants are hazardous; the COSHH controls and specified PPE for that chemical must be used to protect against splashes, fumes and skin or eye contact.

n.1: Smelling the chemical exposes you to hazardous fumes; check the label instead.
n.2: Mixing disinfectant with other chemicals can create dangerous reactions.
n.3: Bare-handed handling risks skin and eye harm; PPE is required.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: An infrequently used outlet is identified during a review of a system. As a remedial control measure to reduce stagnation, the usual action is to:
o: Leave it unused, as unused outlets pose no risk
Cap it and forget about it without any record
Flush it regularly, or remove it if it is genuinely not needed
Increase the water temperature across the whole building instead
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Little-used outlets allow water to stagnate; the remedial action is to flush them regularly to maintain turnover, or to remove redundant ones so they cannot become a source of contamination.

n.1: Capping without record leaves a dead leg that can still hold stagnant water; removal or managed flushing is preferred.
n.3: Raising temperature everywhere does not address stagnation in a specific unused outlet.
n.0: Unused outlets are a recognised risk because water stagnates in them; they must be managed.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: A remedial inspection finds a cross-connection where non-potable water could flow back into the wholesome supply. The correct remedial priority is to:
o: Remove or properly isolate the cross-connection and protect the wholesome supply
Do nothing about it, as backflow is really very unlikely ever to occur here
Note it down for the next annual review and take no further action for now
Add some extra disinfectant into the wholesome supply and simply leave the connection be
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: A cross-connection that risks contaminating the wholesome supply must be removed or properly isolated with suitable backflow protection, as protecting drinking water is a priority remedial action.

n.1: Backflow into the wholesome supply is a serious risk to prevent.
n.2: A contamination risk needs prompt action, not deferral.
n.3: Dosing does not remove the cross-connection or backflow risk.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: At the end of a shift an operative realises they forgot to log a required disinfection check. The honest and correct approach is to:
o: Leave the record blank and just hope that nobody asks about it
Invent a plausible reading so the record simply looks complete
Report the missed check so it can be carried out and recorded
Copy the reading across from a similar check done last month
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Records must be honest and complete. A missed check is reported so it can be carried out and correctly recorded, rather than invented, copied or hidden.

n.0: A blank record with a missed check left unaddressed hides a gap in control.
n.1: Inventing a reading is falsification of a safety record.
n.3: Copying an old reading misrepresents the current state of the system.

Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.q: A disinfection has been completed but the flushing step is skipped and the system is handed back with elevated disinfectant still present. What is the main problem with this?
o: The paperwork will simply look a little untidy at the next audit
The job took slightly longer to finish than the client expected
Users could be exposed to unsafe levels of disinfectant in the water
The disinfectant will slowly improve the taste of the water over time
Cleaning, Disinfection & Remedial Action.w: Skipping the flush leaves elevated disinfectant in the water, so users could be exposed to unsafe chemical levels; the system must be flushed to normal supply quality before use.

n.0: Untidy paperwork is trivial next to the health risk.
n.1: The timing of the job is not the safety issue; user exposure is.
n.3: Elevated disinfectant makes water unsafe, it does not improve taste.
